title: WCU's Tammy James wins the state system's Keeper of the Flame Award
summary: The PASSHE honor recognizes James's three decades of work on keeping students enrolled, including the COMPASS retention program she started in 2019 and the university's new One Stop Student Support Center, which she leads.

title: West Chester Borough Council advances a 12.6% property tax increase
summary: Council voted 4-3 to move the 2027 increase forward, which works out to roughly $178 more a year on a $174,600 assessment. Officials point to rising emergency medical costs and shifting stormwater costs into the general fund; a final vote is set for Dec. 16.

title: County will remember people who died homeless at a Dec. 21 ceremony
summary: The Chester County Partnership to End Homelessness holds its free Homeless Persons' Memorial Day gathering from 4 to 4:45 p.m. on the winter solstice at the Government Services Center, with a Zoom option. Registration is requested.

title: Villa Maria wins the 3A field hockey title; Downingtown West falls in soccer final
summary: Villa Maria jumped to a 3-0 lead and beat Parkland 4-1 Saturday for its first state championship since moving up to Class 3A. Downingtown West's girls soccer team lost the 4A final to Central Bucks East, which won its second straight title.

title: Kimberton Whole Foods plans a Downingtown market
summary: The local grocer is planning a new store at Route 322 and Boot Road, with an opening targeted for fall 2028.

title: WCU holiday concert adds a second show Dec. 5
summary: The Wells School of Music's 105th annual holiday program now runs twice on Saturday, Dec. 5, at 3 and 7:30 p.m. in Asplundh Concert Hall. Tickets are $13.50 and the school suggests buying ahead.
loc: Asplundh Concert Hall, 700 S. High St., West Chester

title: WCU's doctoral psychology program wins federal scholarship money at 10 years
summary: A federal HRSA grant of nearly $650,000 a year for five years will fund $30,300 scholarships for up to 20 PsyD students as the program marks its tenth anniversary.

title: Chester County proposes a 5.29% property tax increase for 2027
summary: Commissioners introduced a preliminary $782.2 million budget on Nov. 18 that would add about $27.30 a year per $100,000 of assessed value, after last year's budget held the rate flat. The final vote is set for Dec. 16 at 10 a.m. at the county building on West Market Street.

title: West Chester Preservation Awards honor restored homes and new carriage houses
summary: The West Chester Downtown Foundation's 15th annual awards recognized the Hanna Darlington house beside the library on North Church Street, a restored 1883 Victorian on Dean Street and new carriage-house units built to match historic blocks. A public mural and a student-curated borough history exhibit were also honored.

title: Hometown Christmas Parade returns Dec. 4 with more marching bands
summary: The chamber's parade steps off at 7 p.m. Friday, Dec. 4, after a 6:30 p.m. lighting of the 28-foot tree at the Historic Chester County Courthouse. Organizers added marching bands this year, and float competitions return.
loc: High and Market streets, West Chester

title: Judge clears Exton Square Mall redevelopment; West Whiteland plans to appeal
summary: A Chester County judge on Nov. 13 overturned the township's 2025 rejection of Abrams Realty's plan to replace most of the mall with homes, shops and offices, keeping Boscov's. Supervisors say they will appeal, while the developer prepares for demolition.

title: Christkindlmarkt brings 100-plus vendors to Gay Street Dec. 12
summary: The seventh annual outdoor holiday market fills Gay and Church streets from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. on Saturday, Dec. 12, with handmade gifts, carolers and music. Santa visits M&T Bank on High Street from 2 to 4 p.m.
loc: Gay and Church streets, West Chester

title: Santa lands by helicopter at the American Helicopter Museum Dec. 12
summary: SantaFest runs 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. with Santa's airborne arrival, photos, crafts and STEM activities. New this year is a family gingerbread-house contest built from cardboard and recycled materials the museum supplies.

title: Six holiday weekends start Nov. 27 with store discounts and free street parking
summary: The Greater West Chester Chamber of Commerce expects about 40,000 visitors for its downtown holiday campaign, which opens Black Friday with many of the roughly 180 shops and restaurants offering 20 to 30 percent off and other promotions. On-street parking is free Nov. 27 through 29, and the program runs through New Year's Day.
